### Deprecate loop, used named functions to recur instead

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2012-07-10 10:10:40 +0200
**Commit:** 7728f3d63027c21607a6e43d6a28ddb6e2439676

The reason for deprecating loops is two fold:

1) It reduces the number of special forms. Special forms usually
   allow a variable number of arguments and have special scoping
   rules and they cannot be overridden or removed;

2) Anonymous looping is highly uncommon in Erlang and slower
   than if we loop using named functions;

loop may be added back in the future as a non special form.

### Adds `to_keyword(record)` function to all records

**Author:** Yurii Rashkovskii <yrashk@spawngrid.com>
**Date:** 2012-05-29 14:32:00 -0700
**Commit:** 243a32f2d160bfc8180240ce60865c0148c7397a

This function can be used to convert any record to a Keyword:

    iex> defrecord A, a: 1, b: 2, c: nil
    nil
    iex> A.new
    A[a: 1, b: 2, c: nil]
    iex> A.new.to_keyword
    [{:a,1},{:b,2},{:c,nil}]
    iex> A.new(c: "a").to_keyword
    [{:a,1},{:b,2},{:c,"a"}]

### Remove special case for specs in elixir_module.erl

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2012-10-05 15:24:11 -0700
**Commit:** 441bf29f1630d30b0bf140a01083045c029ea7df

Previously, since the functions were not concrete
but stubs replaced at compilation time, we had to
special the module definition to not actually include
the specs, which would become compilation errors.

Now we provide a concrete implementation of the
functions and therefore the spec will be available
in the final source. Those implementations are not
actually invoked in practice, since they are still
transformed into erlang ones for performance reasons.

**Date:** 2012-09-13 13:56:43 +0200
**Commit:** 58eea96fc22f2ba0527a699b3731c42af17e72f5

We avoid returning { module, binary, result } because
it can be mistakenly confused as a record named module.

### Reduce atom footprint when compiling code

**Date:** 2012-11-15 16:44:20 +0100
**Commit:** 40efeb48d711c716ade90b00b3216d3a61c2fe87

Previously, we were generating atom names based on
the file or the module name. This commit replaces
it by a pool of atom names. After a module name
is used and purged with success, it is added back
to the pool so it can be reused many times.

### Keep user's given name when rebinding variables

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2012-11-01 11:31:43 +0100
**Commit:** 01f95188993d4ebe763e330cee1cb7c75ce4ce83

The following code:

    counter = 1
    counter = 2

Is now rewritten internally to:

    counter   = 1
    counter@1 = 2

Which gives us a couple things:

1. Better debugging
2. We can now show warnings for rebound variables not used

Elixir also keeps `_@` prefix to store internal variables
(for example, `_@1`, `_@MODULE`, etc).

Closes #607.

**Author:** Yurii Rashkovskii <yrashk@gmail.com>

### Revert "Work around a dialyzer bug"

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2012-10-27 20:56:02 +0200
**Commit:** 94b4831709e992db5c7f3ad5fda19314e16aa0ca

The dialyzer bug was caused because orelse clauses was generated
from inside out. For example, the following clause:

    var in [:a, :b, :c]

Was generating:

    ((var == :a orelse var == :b) orelse var == :c)

Instead of:

    var == :a orelse var == :b orelse var == :c

While it isn't clear why the first one caused the dialyzer to
hang, the `in` operator was fixed to output the second in the
previous commit.

This reverts commit 3c15bcc36f6cd3bfda75c4129a6bea135ac2315d.

### Provide iex -S mix instead of mix iex

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-01-20 12:23:35 -0700
**Commit:** aa9c93305ec27fa22a81b46a92ac7c9a985a8b30

In order for iex to work reliably, we need it to pass special
parameters to the Erlang VM. Therefore, it cannot be started
via a regular Elixir script, as in `mix iex`.

Therefore, we need to use `iex -S mix` which first boots iex
and then run the given mix commands.

Closes #692

### Provide faster record dispatching for protocols that do not have fallbacks.

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-01-06 16:12:12 +0100
**Commit:** 9776f239b4732ecea08725fbb00adbaf5ef9a85d

Currently, if a protocol must be implemented for records but
not for tuples or any other data type, we simply dispatch to
the given tuple, assuming it is valid.

The downside is that we don't show `Protocol.UndefinedError`
messages if the protocol is invalid, but that can easily be
inflected from the underlying UndefinedFunctionError message.

### Add metadata support to ExUnit

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-02-17 18:20:06 -0700
**Commit:** 8f57b4c9afee1946885e6731b6dcfe2440c69b56

Defining setup/teardown/test explicitly is now deprecated.
They should now be defined via their respective macros:

    def setup do
      ...
    end

Now becomes:

    setup do
      ...
    end

When defined using the new format, setup callbacks can
return metadata:

    setup do
      [do_this: :do_that]
    end

And now the test macro can access this metadata:

    test "check metadata", data do
      assert data[:do_this] == :do_that
    end

the original expressions are coming from compared to the
lexical check_clauses field we had in elixir_scope.

A direct consequence of this commit is that, the following
code:

      import List
    end

Now raises a warning if the List import is not used,
where it didn't previously.

### Make String.to_float always return a float

**Author:** J David Eisenberg <jdavid.eisenberg@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2013-05-10 15:06:57 -0700
**Commit:** e40f0c1ec50dd5a0137b2018c399fe50efd8ad09

Added code to make String.to_float("34") return {34.0, ""}

----

### Add String.to_integer/1 and String.to_float/1

**Author:** J David Eisenberg <jdavid.eisenberg@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2013-05-10 11:39:49 -0700
**Commit:** 26aa75318b5606279c4107114b05e97f5ceeb9a0

Given a string that starts with a valid integer, String.to_integer/1
returns a tuple {result, remainder} where remainder is the character
string following the valid integer. If the input is not valid as
specified by Erlang's :string.to_integer/1, the function returns
:error.

Given a string that starts with a valid float, String.to_float/1
returns a tuple {result, remainder} where remainder is the character
string following the valid float. If the input is not valid as
specified by Erlang's :string.to_float/1, the function then calls
String.to_integer/1 and returns that value, which is either an
{integer result, remainder} or :error.

This latter behavior allows you to say String.to_float("34")
without generating an error.

### Improve previous clause does not match warning

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-05-04 14:57:45 -0600
**Commit:** 1019879bd0e43858a9e24495f0906ac776093b08

We have redefined the warning to say:

  "trying to override previously defined function NAME/ARITY"

We have also relaxed the rules that causes the warning to
emitted. For example, if any kind of meta-programming or
unquoting is detected in the function definition, we skip
the warning altogether.

Closes #934.

###  Fixes a bug in Stringends_with?

**Author:** Dave Thomas <dave@pragprog.com>
**Date:** 2013-05-25 17:43:02 -0500
**Commit:** 478f9bbb52f61c115f2790cb7f576f1f2d7908e5

  iex> String.ends_with? "hello", ["hell", "lo"]
  false

 The problem was that the implementation uses :binary.matches, and that returns only
 one match. It would find "hell", but pos+len != size, and so returned false.

 Changed for a less efficient implementation.

### Merge pull request #1177 from fishcakez/hashdict-unordered

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>

Fix HashDict so that key comparison uses exact match
----

### Fix HashDict so that key comparison uses exact match

**Author:** James Fish <james@fishcakez.com>
**Date:** 2013-06-02 21:38:45 +0100
**Commit:** d1fd5a3c2a3b84b993c56bf9871444c5ff0afa59

This change means that HashDict buckets are nolonger strictly ordered.
Previously keys which compared equal (==) but not exactly equal (===)
would be considered different for large sizes but equivalent for small
sizes. This ambiguity occured because hashes are only equal when terms
are exactly equal (===), so both now use exact (===) key comparisons.
Small HashDicts are still a single ordered list and large HashDicts
contain ordered buckets. Both of these may contain keys that compare
equal (==) but are not exactly equal (===), should these keys be present
in the same list or bucket the ordering of these keys (relative to each
other) is undefined.

See github issue #1171 for examples.

Note: If assumptions were made about the form of a HashDict they may
nolonger be valid. Particularly that HashDicts can nolonger be reliably
pattern matched on for equality.

### Move dependencies callbacks back into Mix.Deps.Converger

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-06-01 07:15:51 +0900
**Commit:** f97a384b82d398e26009995aebd5e36aaad29a34

The converger is the one that knows if a dependency exists or
not and, as such, is the best one to know if a dependency callback
should be invoked or not.

This commit also normalizes some of the Retriever internal
functions, for example, now we have mix_children and rebar_children.
The goal is to extract those functions (and the ones in Mix.Deps)
one by one into a Mix.DepsManager behaviour which will be implemented
by Mix.DepsManager.Mix and Mix.DepsManager.Rebar, removing all
the conditional calls existing in the code.

    { :->, meta, list({ list(expr), expr }) }

To:

----

### Improve efficiency of HashDict contract

**Author:** James Fish <james@fishcakez.com>
**Date:** 2013-06-13 17:25:31 +0100
**Commit:** 582e81442289a0c608e64c3466675753daa409da

When contracting in size the HashDict does not need to relocate
(re-hash) key-value pairs. It is not required because each of the
deepest nodes in a trie become a bucket on contraction. This bucket
contains all the key-value pairs in that node.

### Clean up Elixir internal errors

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-07-12 11:30:29 +0200
**Commit:** ebb550008674a25b9928f5e13efea47ed727c1a1

In particular, we reserve SyntaxError for synatx errors (doh)
and for macros that expects a given format at compilation time.

For example, defmodule/2 expects a :do keyword in the second
argument, not providing one is a syntax error.

In other places we impose similar restrictions bue the values
are allowed to be any expression as long as the final result
at compilation time is a given expression, for example:

    when foo in @value

The right side of in can be anything as long it is a list or
a range at compilation time. Those kind of errors are now
CompileError.

### Pretty printer now prints grouped elements in the same line, closes #1383

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-07-09 02:21:55 +0200
**Commit:** 2dc1e41aca4b456ee7644f3c4c97a2205f0df36b

This implementation slightly changes the semantic of Lindig's algorithm
to allow elements that belong to the same group to be printed together
in the same line, even if they do not fit the line fully. This was achieved
by changing `:break` to mean a possible break and `:flat` to force a flat
structure. Then deciding if a break works as a newline is just a matter
of checking if we have enough space until the next break that is not
inside a group (which is still flat).

### Tighten up the grammar rules regarding parentheses omission

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-07-04 18:48:53 +0200
**Commit:** ebe522ec507e2a09190e658ab9f9923b54310f00

Prior to this commit, Elixir allowed too many ambiguous calls
by ommitting the parentheses:

    do_something 1, is_list [], 3
    [1, is_atom :foo, 3]

Both cases above would lead to a compilation error, as an attempt
to call is_list/2 and is_atom/2 would happen. Those examples will
now raise a syntax error, pointing to the ambiguous location.

We have disallowed such examples throughout the language with
the exception of one argument calls:

    assert is_list []

Examples as above are extremely frequent and were kept as is.

**Date:** 2013-06-21 17:51:26 -0300

### using Lindig's strict pretty printer

**Author:** Gustavo Brunoro <brunoro@devio.us>
**Date:** 2013-06-14 15:56:44 -0300
**Commit:** a41528d297d162bcf0b8b5de4a0d71656ea92cca

* Implemented Wadler document algebra with explicit groups, meaning
  that a break should be rendered to a linebreak or a space as
  specified by a mode: `Flat` or `Break`.
* This algorithm reduces the search space for document layouts, as
  no `best` function is used to search lazily over layouts with a
  flat or newline breaks.

### Accept the `trim` option for `Regex.split/3`

**Author:** vanstee <patrick@vanstee.me>
**Date:** 2013-08-25 13:58:42 -0400
**Commit:** e304ea9543b1bc30b8f4e800b135f60819931b68

By default `trim` will be set to true. However, since the `global` option
was implemented with the `parts` option (`{ :parts, :infinity }`), we
have to apply a filter to the final result to support `trim`.

----

### Accept the `trim` option when splitting strings

**Author:** vanstee <patrick@vanstee.me>
**Date:** 2013-08-25 13:36:59 -0400
**Commit:** 64cdc768320f03d33d11dc1acd8a44c7810a0d34

By default `trim` will be set to true. Because `:binary.strip` only
removes empty strings from the end of the result, we have to apply a
filter to remove empty strings from the beginning before returning.

**Commit:** 5bbaeee149a7ce174ea082c76192cdb0fe70c265

children, and not kill it. By killing a supervisor you may prevent the
correct termination of processes further down the supervision tree.

### Add validity checking for Inspect.Algebra documents

### explicitly use `Dict.size` rather than just `size` in `equal?`

**Author:** Julian Doherty (madlep) <madlep@madlep.com>
**Date:** 2013-09-29 22:10:43 +1000
**Commit:** eff51e4045077c5f9c9f5af9e881e9021ea5385d

Fixes bug where `true` was incorrectly returned for `Dict.equal?` when
the 1st argument was a subset of the 2nd argument.

e.g:
```elixir
iex> h1 = HashDict.new(foo: 1, bar: 2)
iex> h2 = HashDict.new(foo: 1, bar: 2, baz: 3)
iex> Dict.equal?(h1, h2)
true # OOPS
iex> Dict.equal?(h2, h1)
false # works as expected other way round
```

The code to check equality was checking size (incorrectly), and then
checking to see if every element in the first dict was present in the
2nd.

However, `size` was being used instead of `Dict.size`. This ended up
calling `Kernel.size` instead - and would always return `true`
regardless of whever the actual size of the `Dict` arguments were the
same or not.

### Support String.split with an empty binary as the pattern.

**Author:** Bruce Williams <brwcodes@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2013-09-06 16:19:40 -0700
**Commit:** 0e725fb906c1532d2dac29aa66dec0f8707c0865

As discussed in #1688, currently the following fails:

    iex> String.split "abc", ""
    ** (ArgumentError) argument error
        binary.erl:242: :binary.split/3

These changes add support for an empty binary pattern, piggybacking on
the empty regular expression split (vs using `String.graphemes`,
notably) so that the function continues to support the `:global`
option.

Users should probably be using `String.graphemes` for splitting, but
this keeps the API consistent while fixing this exception.

Closes #1688.

Conflicts:
	lib/elixir/lib/string.ex

### fix wrong error message for `nil.func()` call

**Author:** Samuel Tonini <tonini.samuel@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2013-10-31 15:31:35 +0100
**Commit:** 2e9f4196cd8ca8f42664bb69cfc1bd5acf6e895f

The expected behavior for `nil.func()` should be:

    iex(1)> nil.test()
    ** (UndefinedFunctionError) undefined function: nil.test/0
       nil.test()

Also via cli `elixir -e`:

     $ elixir -e 'nil.test()'
     ** (UndefinedFunctionError) undefined function: nil.test/0
     nil.test()
     ....

Undefined function calls behave like:

    iex(1)> hello()
    ** (RuntimeError) undefined function: hello/0

### Same module variables must be explicitly shared

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-10-30 14:53:36 +0100
**Commit:** f1e2fcf9f9ed5bca922f8c041c116fcd989a3b73

Prior to this commit, the following code would work:

    defmodule Hello do
      defmacro write do
        quote do
          a = 1
        end
      end

      defmacro read do
        quote do
          a
        end
      end
    end

    require Hello
    Hello.write
    Hello.read

Although this is convenient, it has many issues:

1. It is not clear at any point the intent of sharing the variables
   in between the macros

2. Whenever macros from the same module are nested, there is a chance
   a variable used before and after the nesting to be overriden

We address this issue by only allowing variables explicitly marked
with var! to be shared. Here is how the example above should be updated:

    defmodule Hello do
      defmacro write do
        quote do
          var!(a, Hello) = 1
        end
      end

      defmacro read do
        quote do
          var!(a, Hello)
        end
      end
    end

    require Hello
    Hello.write
    Hello.read

We have used the following commands to compile those files
with the appropriate optimization info:

    ERL_COMPILER_OPTIONS="bin_opt_info" elixir lib/elixir/lib/integer.ex
    ERL_COMPILER_OPTIONS="bin_opt_info" elixir lib/elixir/lib/float.ex

Implement protocol consolidation
----

### Remove @prioritize from Protocols

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-10-10 11:55:28 +0200
**Commit:** fad38e1bab9946c195b2f07a8b2239f2b35b2d12

The consolidation algorithm is now fast enough that prioritize
does not actually make any difference in performance. We achived
that by compiling the dispatch in two set of functions: one that
checks the types (list, tuple, function, etc) and another that
checks the leading atom name for records (HashDict, HashSet, etc).

By breaking in two different sets, the Erlang compiler can better
optimize pattern matching on those items to the point prioritizing
does not yield any benefit.

Thanks to @ericmj for the initial suggestion.

Based on a suggestion @krestenkrab and an initial implementation
proposed in #1902, we can reduce the total size of the String.Graphemes
beam file by ensuring the function clauses for next_grapheme are
similar.

We have done this by implementing next_grapheme in a tail recursive
fashion and using binary_part to select the first bits. The end result
is a consistently 33% faster graphemes operation for ascii strings
and only 10% slower operation for heavy unicode strings (which may
be further optimazable).

pad is given, you get an extra element.

Enum.chunks([1,2,3], 3)
iex> [[1,2,3]]

iex> [[1,2,3],[""]]
as not expected

### Merge pull request #1893 from elixir-lang/jv-ex-in-ex

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-11-24 04:44:42 -0800
**Commit:** 08afaa7982ba5931c3d96e698fdb22aaff94c165

This merge moves most of the macros implemented in erlang to elixir.

The exceptions are `case/2`, `try/2` and `receive/1` that cannot be written
in Elixir and therefore were converted to special forms.

On the plus side, `var!/1`, `var!/2` and `alias!/1` were converted to regular
macros (and demoted from special forms).

This also simplifies dispatching, as we no longer need to special case
some of the Kernel macros.

### Improve error message for IEx.Helpers.r when module does not exist.

**Author:** Ricardo de Cillo <ricardo.cillo@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-12-30 01:56:55 -0200
**Commit:** ddd4afbdbab9aebbcc18191afdff1ce5d1a2a3be

Before this commit, when trying to reload an unloaded module, the
user would see an error like:

iex(1)> r InexistentModule
** (UndefinedFunctionError) undefined function: InexistentModule.module_info/1
    InexistentModule.module_info(:compile)
    lib/iex/lib/iex/helpers.ex:352: IEx.Helpers.source/1
    lib/iex/lib/iex/helpers.ex:311: IEx.Helpers.do_r/1
    lib/iex/lib/iex/helpers.ex:304: IEx.Helpers.r/1

After this commit, the user should see


iex(1)> r InexistentModule
** (ArgumentError) Unloaded module Elixir.InexistentModule. Try loading the module's beam file with `IEx.Helpers.l\1`
    lib/iex/lib/iex/helpers.ex:312: IEx.Helpers.do_r/1
    lib/iex/lib/iex/helpers.ex:304: IEx.Helpers.r/1

Which is more informative.

### Change how -> is represented in the AST

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-12-23 16:10:33 +0100
**Commit:** 51aef55c830b770d85c1add1eccd6dcb440fd018

The previous representation was very hard to compose
and very often required the AST nodes to be created
manually.

The current approach is easier to compose because
the node is represented as any other operator as long
as it is wrapped in parentheses.

For example, imagine we have pairs of patterns and
the code to be executed for that pattern, and we want
to inject them into a case. It can now be writen as:

    pairs = Enum.map pairs, fn { pattern, expr } ->
      quote do: (unquote(pattern) -> unquote(expr))
    end

    quote do
      case unquote(condition), do: unquote(pairs)
    end

Compare to the previous implementation:

    pairs = Enum.map pairs, fn { pattern, expr } ->
      { [pattern], [], expr }
    end

    pairs = { :->, [], pairs }

    quote do
      case unquote(condition), do: unquote(pairs)
    end

### Improve compilation times and memory consumption

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2013-12-21 20:06:50 +0100
**Commit:** c7af8bc2cc32e8bd5bc08af13d4dffc42063b386

This commit includes three changes:

1. Previously, the parallel compiler released at once all processes
   depending on a particular module. This commit ensures they are
   released according to the number of cores available. This ensures
   we have fewer modules being compiled at once

2. Garbage collect the current process every time we are waiting
   for another module to be compiled

3. Do not compile a module for files that simply define modules

### Deprecate Enum.first/1 in favor of Enum.at/2 and List.first/1

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2014-01-14 16:26:30 +0100
**Commit:** 42fc70a0eb66315f79acbc491d61d23e600d2a11

The main reason for this change is because `Enum.first/1` does
not communicate that enumeration will happen, in contrast to
functions like Enum.at/2 and Enum.fetch/2 which are meant to
be used with non-indexed collections and the need for enumeration
is made a bit more obvious.

Closes #1983

### Remove Unix specific behaviour from File.cp/3 and File.cr_r/3

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2014-01-30 09:57:48 +0100
**Commit:** 2da92475ba5893630105edf68eaf6e317190252b

Previously those functions would behave as in their Unix counterpart
where copying behaved differently depending if the destination was
an existing directory or not. We have explicitly disallowed this
behaviour and added the proper notes to the docs.

### Change HashDict implementation to use tries with compound nodes

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2014-01-19 13:58:45 +0100
**Commit:** d311e10bea0f254ebde7ccc378d025a72defcd36

The new implementation is basically a tree of tuples (tries) but
they allow compond nodes (a node with a key-value pair and a
sub-tree). This removes the need for node-expansion and also simplifies
the design structure to not require multiple stages nor buckets.

The end result is a faster HashDict implementation (about 10% faster
on access, 30% on updates), which is still small for small dicts
but about 30% bigger for large dicts (in terms of memory) and with
a much simpler implementation.

Those warnings happen because we need to test basic functionality,
like `nil?(nil) == true` and the Erlang compiler can see this
expression will always work.

We can work around this issue by adding a bit of indirection, like
`nil?(List.first([nil])) == true`.

    iex(77)> String.slice("string", 1..-2)
    "trin"
    iex(78)> String.slice("string", -5..-2)
    "trin"

### Test git in dep folder to consider checked out

**Author:** Andreas Amsenius <andreas@amsenius.se>
**Date:** 2014-05-01 23:16:03 +0200
**Commit:** 2b1f561d91990eeb8dbac66d136b4aeaca377e0c

If the .git folder of a dep becomes corrupted, any git command
issued by mix could find a parent .git folder and wipe the parent
tree.

This fix only consider a git dependency checked out if git is able
to read the .git folder.

Signed-off-by: José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>

### Rename the `args` variable to `attrs` or `opts` where appropriate

**Author:** Alexei Sholik <alcosholik@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2014-04-28 01:54:44 +0300
**Commit:** f3bbb1ea439df71c7dd9f8a1b375a28cf5f5c658

It is a good convention to have the name "args" refer to variables
that actually contain a list of arguments dispatched to a function
in some way.

When passing a keyword list to a record constructor,
it is referred to as "attributes" or "attrs".

When passing a list of arbitrary options,
it is referred to as "opts".

**Commit:** 29e0fadec143ec0123bf550656e19bd6be1d78b2

Previously the source filename of a module was sometimes a binary, this
change ensures it is always an erlang string.

Previously dialyzer did not know not to auto import bifs as it does not
read the compile options from a beam. This change uses an attribute in
the abstract code rather than a compile option so that dialyzer does not
auto import bifs.

### Fix ordered list formatting

**Author:** Alexei Sholik <alcosholik@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2014-06-17 02:52:05 +0300
**Commit:** 41c74e96824b1a64379d936ebe486f9e3f371bc7

The rules are similar to those for the unordered lists (see previous
commits). Subsequent lines and paragraphs should be aligned to the
beginning of the sentence on the first line, like this:

  1. This is a list item,
     it has a second line.

     Also paragraph.

  2. Second list item.

         code fragment

Short, one-sentence items that can be read as part of the surrounding
paragraph can start with a non-capital letter
----

### Apply uniform capitalization and punctuation rules to all lists

**Author:** Alexei Sholik <alcosholik@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2014-06-17 16:25:16 +0300
**Commit:** e0f5dd506ab10b2b2f9225698ff56cd54a6f5400

  * Never use capital letters after `-`. Sentences start right after
    the bullet and continue to the first period.

  * When list elements are one or two sentences, use non-capitalized
    format without terminators.

    The two sentences are converted into one, separated by a semicolon.
    This mainly applies to the cases with short sentences or when only
    one of many list elements needs to have two sentences.

    Example:

        * `:opt_a` - basic description, no terminator
        * `:opt_b` - also short description; this used to be second
          sentence

  * When at least one list element needs to have real sentences, 
    the whole list is formatted like that, with a period at the end
    of each element:

        * `:opt_a` - this is still short.

        * `:opt_b` or `:opt_c` - but this is longer. May have multiple 
          sentences.

          Or even paragraphs.

### Reformat unordered lists in all docstrings

**Author:** Alexei Sholik <alcosholik@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2014-06-17 02:01:27 +0300
**Commit:** 915ba1bb298f2c0b11c92eefd7f9dfe0a8677f96

List items are marked with a star (*). Bullets marking list elements
must have a 2-space indent. The continuation lines should be indented
by 2 more spaces.

The second and subsequent paragraphs need to be indented 4 spaces
from the beginning of the line to be included in the list item.

The code fragments have to be indented 8 spaces from the beginning
of the line (or 4 spaces from the beginning of the preceding paragraph).

Sublists are marked with a hyphen (-). They follow the rules above
with the difference that their initial indent will be greater
(8 spaces from the beginning of the line).
----

### Kill test process only after on_exit runs

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2014-06-10 12:03:19 +0200
**Commit:** 6e9f9f254f433d1d0bd517ab6744e78b84e1a8db

We do this to avoid links created during the test from
crashing when the test exits which happened before the on_exit
callbacks run.

This was particularly troubling with GenServer, GenEvent
and Supervisor, in which the first does not crash when
a linked process exits with normal reason, but the other
two do. Due to this behaviour, before this change there was
a possibility of race conditions causing tests to crash on
on_exit.

In case the test process exits with a non-normal reason,
all links will be broken, so the problem doesn't manifest
in such cases.

### Set :proc_lib initial call on task

**Author:** James Fish <james@fishcakez.com>
**Date:** 2014-06-18 22:58:20 +0100
**Commit:** 7123fb9d09d2df4b5e940688ce9ae9608166c542

Sets the :proc_lib initial call to the {mod, fun, arity} of the task.

This allows :proc_lib.translate_initial_call(task.pid) to show the mfa
of a task process when debugging. Tools such as :observer and the erlang
shell make use of this function when getting information on a process.

This gives a useful initial call in the crash report sent to the error
logger when a task raises.

**Date:** 2014-06-28 17:23:46 -0500
**Commit:** 0bdee49f7f216e4536b0486ce2f8506073d0629c

Enum.sort_by/3 takes a collection, a mapper function, an an optional
sorter function.  The function sorts by the mapped value using the sorter.
The optional sorter default to `<=/2`.

### Introduce new operators intended for use by parser combinator libraries.

**Author:** Alex Rønne Petersen <alex@lycus.org>
**Date:** 2014-08-21 03:05:14 +0200
**Commit:** c8bcd89c7c6abed0e899a2adc305779412c33a8d

The expected definitions (which are by no means required) in
parser combinator speak are:

* `p  ~>> f`   =  `bind(p, f)`
* `p1 ~>  p2`  =  `pair_right(p1, p2)`
* `p1 <~  p2`  =  `pair_left(p1, p2)`
* `p1 <~> p2`  =  `pair_both(p1, p2)`
* `p  |~> f`   =  `map(p, f)`
* `1p <|> p2`  =  `either(p1, p2)`

### Fix logger watcher race condition

**Author:** James Fish <james@fishcakez.com>
**Date:** 2014-08-23 17:50:39 +0100
**Commit:** c0a075724f678bbc2c82737acf77b43eb8b85bf6

Previously a backend could be removed from logger and the watcher would
not have exited before the remove_backend/1 call returned. This meant
that a new watcher could not always be started because the child
(watcher) might still exist but be about to die.

----

to the caller to decide.

**Commit:** d9125b0a81173a9760f7b6063c724bb8527f9998

processes and the module definition could leave stale data
in the elixir_modules table.

The issue has been fixed by emitting the proper exit signals
and by using monitors.

### Make a distinction between touching and updating the lock manifest

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-09-17 12:40:44 +0200
**Commit:** 25b813c4e62520ab60a903c11e464c17e34ffcf0

Previously, deps.compile would update the parent project
lock manifest, which updated its Elixir version and made
it impossible to detect later on that we were upgrading
from a previous Elixir version.

This commit adds the ability to both touch and update
the manifest file and change deps.compile to only touch
it.

### Use multiline failure message for asser_raise/3

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-09-13 11:37:51 +0200
**Commit:** db93099120fdaad018d7d90c6e197fa9c0ba65f2

Before this commit, `assert_raise/3` in ExUnit used an uncomfortable
failure message when the expected exception message and the real one
didn't match: they were both written on the same line, which caused
problems for long-ish messages.

Now, each exception message is printed on its own line, which should
make it clearer to spot differences and cleaner in general.

### Fix bugs involving Markdown code

**Author:** eksperimental <eksperimental@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2015-09-11 15:06:52 +0700
**Commit:** eca59aad1700526f4ece1f839aadd5455880fd47

Fix common mistakes like the random backtick hanging in the wrong place,
or the wrongly formatted link, or single-quotes instead of backtick.

Commands to detect these common mistakes:
        ## COMMON MISTAKES
        # single backtick in html docs
        ag '`' ./doc --ignore "*.css" --ignore "*.js"
        # links in the wrong format
        ag '\[\w+://[^)\] ]+\]'
        ag '\(\w+://[^)\] ]+\]'
        ag '\[\w+://[^)\] ]+\)'
        # find html code like: ["Strictly Pretty" (2000) by Christian Lindig][0]</p>
        ag '\[[^\]]+\](\(|\[)' doc/ --ignore "*.js"

----

### Standardize use of backticks and quotes; including Error messages and Title Case commands

**Author:** eksperimental <eksperimental@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2015-09-09 12:35:17 +0700
**Commit:** ed5671b4f8c44581d1b0e472196903bbc7452655

This is a large commit that does the following:
* Removes backticks from messages and comments.
  All references to backticks have been replaced with double quotes everywhere the
  code is not interpreted as Markdown, (ie. anywhere outside documentation and
  markdown files, such as in code comments, or error messages).

* Variables in Exception messages are printed using `inspect`
  The way no-matching error message are printed, have changed because now we use inspect for printing
  variables. The following file and their respective test have been changed:
  - lib/elixir/lib/exception.ex
  - lib/elixir/lib/inspect/algebra.ex
  - lib/elixir/test/elixir/inspect_test.exs
  - lib/ex_unit/test/ex_unit/formatter_test.exs
  - lib/elixir/test/elixir/exception_test.exs

* Properly use Title Case for Mix, Git, Dializer

* Use backticks when citing a command

****************************************************
CONVENTION FOR RENAMING USING BACKTICKS AND QUOTES

https://github.com/elixir-lang/elixir/pull/3697#issuecomment-138811747

1. Backticks should never be printed in error messages, neither be included anywhere where Markdown code is not interpreted as such.

2. Do not use single quotes anywhere. We should favor double quotes everywhere, to avoid confusion

3. If you want to format something in error messages, use inspect. For example, if you want to show the dependency name and that is an atom, instead of the dependency "foo", let's show the dependency :foo. Less noise and may click better

4. Similarly, if you want to show something with double quotes, call inspect, as it handles escaping as well as the quotes

5. Things like "--all" just add verbosity, we can definitely read --all without ambiguity.

6. When using switches with a single hyphen (such as "-o"), we can make it explicit in the text: e.g. "... give the switch -o when choosing ..."

****************************************************
SHELL COMMANDS TO DETECT CODE BREAKING THE RULES

* Detect values surrounded by single-quotes where we want double-quotes.

    # regular variables
    ag "'#{"
    # constants or ENV variables
    ag "'[A-Z][A-Z0-9_-]+"
    # switches
    ag -i "(?<!(\[))'--?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]+'"
    # atoms
    ag -i "(?<!(\[))':[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]+'"

    # DETECT BACKTICKS OUTSIDE DOCS
    ag "^\s+(?<!(#))#[^#\r\n]*\`" --ignore "*.md"
    ag '^\s+["%].*`' --ignore "*.md"
    ag -s '(raise|Error)\b(?!(`|/)).*\`'

* Spot mentions to running a command that is not using backticks:

    commands="elixir|elixirc|mix|iex|ex_doc|git|make|rebar|dialyzer|erl|rm|cd|mkdir|rmdir|ln|ls|pwd"
    actions="runs?|running|executes?|executing|types?|typing|enters?|entering|calls?|calling"
    ag '(?i)('${actions}')(?-i)\b[^`\r\n/]+[\ \t]+(?!(`))('${commands}')'
    ag '(?-i)\b(?!(`))('${commands}')[\ \t]+[^`\r\n/]+(?i)(commands?)'

* Spot where a command is mentioned:

    #commands="erlang|elixir|eex|iex|ex_unit|ex_doc|logger|elixirc|git|make|rebar|dialyzer|erl|rm|cd|mkdir|rmdir|ln|ls|pwd"
    commands="mix|elixirc|git|make|rebar|dialyzer|erl|rm|cd|mkdir|rmdir|ln|ls|pwd"
    ag -s '(?<!(\`))(?<!(\.))(?<!(/))(?<!(:))(?<!(_))\b('${commands}')\b(?!(:))(?!(\?))(?!(_))(?!(-))(?!(\.))(?!(\`))(?!(/))(?!(>))' \
    --ignore "*.erl" --ignore "*.yrl" --ignore "*.src"

----

**Commit:** 06d94f5b90c2ddefbfb445cad5634a9829b897c2

This commits covers 100% of all links in the documentation,
using a words to describe what the page is about.

It users the `:module.function/arity` format for erlang functions that
link to the earlang docs.

I also changed some of the sentnces using the link from
- See [:erlang.function/2](http://...) for a list of available options.

to
- For a list of available options, see [:erlang.function/2](http://...)

The reasoning behind is that I think it's better to have an link at the end of the sentence
and not in the middle, so the reades doesn't need to finish the sentence to know what is it about and go back
and find the link. This way all the information is given before the link, so the users stops reading and can
click directly.

Format raise message consistently
----

### Format raise message consistently

**Author:** eksperimental <eksperimental@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2015-09-08 00:23:14 +0700
**Commit:** a251ccc722a3736a5a5f79edcb69b5fb749b3738

Kernel.raise messages should not start with uppercase, and should not
have trailing punctuation.

Mix.raise messages should start with uppercase, and should not have a trailing
puntuation.

    # starting with uppercase
    # exclude (Mix.raise, and any message that starts with all uppecase such as: I or IO
    ag '(?<!Mix\.)raise\s+\"+(?!([A-Z]+\b))[A-Z]'

    # Mix.raise should start with upper case
    # except when `mix` or `rebar` are mentioned
    ag 'Mix\.raise\s+\"(?!(mix|rebar))+[a-z]'

    # ending in period
    ag "raise\s+\"+.+\.\"\s*\n"

### Correct descriptions in @doc, @moduledoc, @shortdoc to use Present Continuous

**Author:** eksperimental <eksperimental@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2015-09-07 18:16:21 +0700
**Commit:** 8d5c009b13f01a23a7b396407d4541405e69432d

It makes it consistent with the rest of the docs.

I have just looked for the first line in @doc, @moduledoc, so lines bellow it may still need
to be corrected.

@shortdoc all have been corrected.

Inspired by: https://github.com/elixir-lang/elixir/pull/2942

Command to list the first lines:

```sh
  # first line in @moduledoc / @doc
  ag '(@(module)?doc)\s+("{3})(\r|\n|.)\s*+[\w-]+(?<!s)\b'

  # also @shortdoc
  ag '(@shortdoc)\s+("{1,3})(\r|\n|.)\s*+[\w-]+(?<!s)\b'
```

**Author:** Gary Rennie <gazler@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-08-24 23:41:11 +0100
**Commit:** c53da7ae12d7ce3ebbdceb047a1062369cffb20b

`Kernel.if` and `Kernel.unless` are now only valid if there is exactly
one `do` key and optionally an `else` key.

Any calls to the if macro that do not satisfy these conditions raise an
ArgumentError with a relevant error message.

This closes #3614

### doctests raising exceptions and assert_raise show original stacktrace

**Author:** Abel Muiño <amuino@1uptalent.com>
**Date:** 2015-08-08 12:53:48 +0200
**Commit:** fe4c851424fefb09aae9ac09d9650a3d1a299f69

Currently doctests report the type and message of the raised exception,
but a synthetic stacktrace.
`assert_raise` does not provide any information about why
the wrong exception was raised, since the stacktrace points to test
line.

This change makes it display the original stacktrace too, which is more
useful for debugging and keeps symmetry with the information that
standard ExTests provide.

### Optimize many functions in String

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-08-02 13:49:43 +0200
**Commit:** 0e7232671b394637e3da0267c01594820f7917e6

Many functions relied on next_grapheme, which would traverse
the whole string generating a lot of graphemes as garbage along
the way.

This commit introduces next_grapheme_size, which returns the
size in bytes of the next grapheme, avoiding the generation
of the garbage and optimizing functions that need just the
byte_size.

Functions optimized are: String.at, String.split_at, String.slice
and String.length.

### Streamline aliases and imports in lexical tracker

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-07-22 09:59:31 +0200
**Commit:** 80fd98f01afbf9118e6dc64b82441229da2f9909

Aliases should not mark nodes as compile or runtime
since it receives the alias to be expanded. The
expanded alias is always called later though as a
remote dispatch.

Imports should always mark nodes as compile time,
since they are compile time dependencies.

Finally, ensure compile nodes have higher priority
over runtime ones.

----

### Reduce noise in lexical tracker output

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-07-22 02:53:25 +0200
**Commit:** 1fd72ba72f94c96d56a308539184bffdaebdd723


----

### Only recompile compile time dependencies in mix projects

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-07-22 01:19:57 +0200
**Commit:** 7e0ecec061afcc0f437944daa4ef74b42cec935d

Prior to this patch, if module A invoked B, regardless of
where, A would recompile if B was changed.

Since the previous commit, we are now able to distinguish
between compile time dependencies (macros and calls outside
of a function) from runtime ones (everything else).

Now when traversing the dependency tree, runtime dependencies
since marks a given module as stale. If there is, however, a
compile time dependency on any stale module, the module that
depends on the stale dependency is recompiled.

To be more precise, imagine this flow:

    A [calls macro in] B [calls function in] C

Previously, A, B and C would recompile if C changed. Now only
A will.

----

### Move terminate reason to second line in logs

**Author:** James Fish <james@fishcakez.com>
**Date:** 2015-06-19 23:53:12 +0100
**Commit:** 6cd1478a2ec1a3dad7f02fb5b9291abe3a3a427f

With default settings logger could truncate the log before the
terminate reason if there is a large term beforehand, such as a large
message in a GenServer termination report. Therefore move terminate
reason (the most important information) as near the front of the
message as possible so that as little of it as possible is truncated.

`surround_many/5` handles empty documents
----

### `surround_many/5` handles empty documents

**Author:** gabriele.lana <gabriele.lana@cleancode.it>
**Date:** 2015-05-27 06:56:10 +0200
**Commit:** feacf14a352ae19adba7a5352a7a23d732e69392

`surround/3` correctly handles empty documents, ex

    iex> doc = Inspect.Algebra.surround "[", Inspect.Algebra.empty, "]"
    iex> Inspect.Algebra.format(doc, 80) |> IO.iodata_to_binary
    "[]"

But `surround_many/5` didn't

    iex> fun = fn(d, _) -> d end
    iex> opts = %Inspect.Opts{}
    iex> what = ["a", Inspect.Algebra.empty]
    iex> doc = Inspect.Algebra.surround_many("[", what, "]", opts, fun, ",")
    iex> Inspect.Algebra.format(doc, 80) |> IO.iodata_to_binary
    "[a, ]"

This is what I expect and what it does now

    iex> doc = Inspect.Algebra.surround_many("[", what, "]", opts, fun, ",")
    iex> Inspect.Algebra.format(doc, 80) |> IO.iodata_to_binary
    "[a]"

### Merge pull request #3302 from whatyouhide/mix-config-agent

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>

Use agents to store Mix config
----

### Use agents to store Mix config

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-05-02 23:50:11 +0200
**Commit:** da1002257cca2841977eaf86de63851e36381619

Mix config was stored in a variable (`var!(config, Mix.Config)`) which was
initialized at every `use Mix.Config`. Using a variable worked well but didn't
allow pretty much anything outside "straight" code. For example, you could do
this:

    config :foo, bar: :baz

    if 3 + 2 == 5
      config :foo, [math: :check]
    end

but you could not do this:

    f = fn ->
      config :foo, bar: :baz
    end
    f.()

since functions can't leak their scope into the outside scope, so changes to the
`config` variable were not "persisted". `for` comprehensions were not allowed in
the same way.

This commit introduces a `Mix.Config.Agent` module so that configuration can be
stored inside an agent. An agent is started every time that `use Mix.Config` is
called, and is stopped by `Mix.Config.read!/1` (which is the basic unit for
reading configuration; everything else should use it).

### Fix inferred argument names in `Module.simplify_signature/2`

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-04-28 16:33:17 +0200
**Commit:** 34af7baf2df87306cd747a3f06bd091a62a42f17

Arguments like literals (e.g., `4`) were converted into variables like `int1`.
This commit changes this behaviour by adding an index only if necessary (i.e.,
there are duplicates in the signature). For example:

    def foo([], 1, %{}, 2)

becomes

    def foo(list, int1, map, int2)

### Implement `Tuple.append/2`

**Author:** Slava Pavlutin <sl.pavlutin@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-04-10 19:42:53 +0300
**Commit:** 30da6d26d568e945ff8ce3f5fbbfeeff8a8a561b

`Tuple.append/2` adds an element to the end of a tuple, which
mirrors what Erlang's `append_element/2` does. Therefore,
`Tuple.append/2` is implemented to maintain consistency of the API.

Refactor File! methods to avoid going through IO.chardata_to_string twice
----

### Refactor File! methods to avoid going through IO.chardata_to_string twice

**Author:** Carlos Antonio da Silva <carlosantoniodasilva@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-04-10 15:33:30 -0300
**Commit:** 11724d3b11485dff0fd38e2951a8adfb638ead44

All the non-! methods pass the pass argument through IO.chardata_to_string,
and we are doing this work twice for the ! methods since we convert once
before delegating to the non-! versions.

This moves the conversion to the exception case only, which should be
far less common, thus avoiding going through the duplicated call.

### No longer translate arguments to `@on_definition`

**Author:** Or Neeman <oneeman@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-04-04 16:05:12 -0600
**Commit:** ef8dc3c05245d2cdfdb241cfabd36e39fcc39ecf

Breaking change: the arguments to the `@on_definition` hook are no
longer expanded and translated, but are passed in their original quoted
form.  The only exception is module attributes (e.g. `@my_constant`),
which are expanded.

The reason for this change is that this hook is used for generating
functions' documentation, and the previous behavior was causing
incorrect signatures in the documentation.  See #3143 for details.

Closes #3143

**Commit:** babe8f7364fc83c3a05c48114006fd865e458a63

Unreachable private functions are excluded during
compilation. As a result, if such a function had a `@spec`,
it would cause a `CompileError`. This commit fixes that by
also excluding any specs for unreachable private functions.

Closes #3144

### EEx: Add trim option

**Author:** Or Neeman <oneeman@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-03-22 18:18:41 -0600
**Commit:** d90f6ed85870a52f5e143f82888fabb865670452

If the `trim` option is used, trims around EEx tags:
- On left, up to the line break if all whitespace
- On right, up to and including the line break if all whitespace

Does not trim around quotations (`<%% %>`), but does trim around
any tags inside a quotation.

Closes #3154

Fix doctest :only, so it accepts multiple functions
----

### Fix doctest :only, so it accepts multiple functions

**Author:** Martin Svalin <martin@lite.nu>
**Date:** 2015-03-15 02:09:03 +0100
**Commit:** 469017b6c1de40d36343a1664ab98ebd26dfea57

There is a bug in `doctest` with the `:only` option, such that it only works if
the list is of size 1. If you pass two functions to the option, `filter_by_opts`
will always be empty, since the function is checked with `Enum.all?`.

`Enum.any?` returns false for an empty list. Thus the extra `Enum.empty?` check.

This pull request has broken the following expression:

    assert [] = TestRepo.all from p in Post, where: p.title in ^[]

Previously it was parsed as:

    assert [] = TestRepo.all(from p in Post, where: p.title in ^[])

But after this pull request it is parsed as:

    assert [] = TestRepo.all from(p in Post), where: p.title in ^[]

This reverts commit 7f528aa1c035bf5f0e62fe20b6e3975c0084f395, reversing
changes made to 98746e08eaa2bf58c202e8500b6cf83ed2368cc0.

Conflicts:
	lib/elixir/src/elixir_parser.yrl

### Add an :optional option to IEx.Helpers.import_file/1

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-02-11 12:37:46 +0100
**Commit:** ca4161146be3e1e8201b1d66fdbc5f5453457b3c

Added an `:optional` option to the `IEx.Helpers.import_file/1` macro which tells
the macro not to raise exceptions if the given file is missing. This is useful
when one wants to import a file but isn't sure that the file exists (a common
use case is to check for `~/.iex.exs` in a local `.iex.exs`):

    import_file "~/.iex.exs", optional: true

### Logger: Format OTP 17.4 terminate reasons

**Author:** James Fish <james@fishcakez.com>
**Date:** 2015-02-10 20:12:43 +0000
**Commit:** 897359a5238736d989a6989eb6e0b392ecb6aea6

From 17.4 OTP behaviours include the stacktrace in the logged reason
when exit/1 is called. If an elixir exception is raised, or the reason
can be normalized to an elixir exception (not ErlangError), the
exception is formatted as an exception:
** (Exception) message
Otherwise the reason is formatted using Exception.format_exit/1:
** (stop) :reason

**Date:** 2015-02-03 17:00:11 +0100
**Commit:** 478215d60ffc7ed27f2efb4786e9ecb349ab1849

When `raise/1` (or `reraise/2`) is called with an invalid argument (not a module
name neither a binary message), a cryptic `CaseClauseError` is raised. This
behaviour exposes the underlying implementation details of the `raise/1` (or
`reraise/2`) macro.

### Introduce an implementation of Integer.digits/1

**Author:** Matthew Rothenberg <mrothenberg@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2014-12-01 20:05:54 -0500
**Commit:** 825fa7ac4d3d7d156058c1f1b1b02e4a59798de0

Introduces an efficient (purely mathematical) implementation of
Integer.digits/1.

Most developers tend to implement the digits of an integer by converting
to a string representation, splitting the string, and then converting
each char back into an integer.  E.g. with code such as the following:

```elixir
def digits(n) when is_integer(n) and n>0 do
    n
    |> Integer.to_string
    |> String.graphemes
    |> Enum.map(&String.to_integer/1)
end
```
Which results in a lot of inefficient type conversion and memory
allocation.

This implementation is purely mathematical.  In informal benchmarks on
my workstation, it performs at 0.9 μs/op versus 4.8 μs/op in the naïve
implementation above.

----

OTP. Another process is only used if there is no connection the node and
only casts to other nodes are not guaranteed to arrive in order.

Make IO.ANSI.Docs readable on white background
----

### Make IO.ANSI.Docs readable on white background

**Author:** Martin Frost <frost@ceri.se>
**Date:** 2014-11-03 15:33:12 +0100
**Commit:** df44ad4fb2f8caf607e00d05147947d23ed8e1a3

The `default_options` for `IO.ANSI.Docs` uses bright yellow for
documentation headers and titles.

This is very nice and readable when using a terminal with a dark
background. However, when using a terminal with a bright (e.g. white)
background, those parts are unfortunately illegible.

This patch removes the `:bright` part from the `default_options`, to
make the defaults better suited to more people.

  attributes altogether and using table looks for retriving the relevant
  information

  one for data, another for functions and another for clauses

### Merge pull request #4067 from vanstee/allow-false-value-in-env

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>

**Commit:** adaceb36ebd9d870f76c5ec81dcf96fab43d6f8d

Allow `false` value in env passed to `System.cmd/3`
----

### Allow `false` value in env passed to `System.cmd/3`

**Author:** vanstee <patrick@vanstee.me>
**Date:** 2015-12-08 18:43:07 -0500
**Commit:** 966c8a27aec8f9db9febae5befe050209e82b5ff

Previously only strings were accepted as valid env keys and values.
However, because the `env` option is eventually passed to
`:erlang.open_port`, `false` values, which remove existing environment
variables, should be allowed.

From the docs for [`erlang:open_port/2`](http://www.erlang.org/doc/man/erlang.html#open_port-2):

    {env, Env}
      This is only valid for {spawn, Command} and {spawn_executable,
      FileName}. The environment of the started process is extended using the
      environment specifications in Env.

      Env should be a list of tuples {Name, Val}, where Name is the name of an
      environment variable, and Val is the value it is to have in the spawned
      port process. Both Name and Val must be strings. The one exception is
      Val being the atom false (in analogy with os:getenv/1), which removes
      the environment variable.

### Do not check for configured apps when build path is set

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-11-28 12:55:06 +0100
**Commit:** 7963398aaf448f7113b94ecd27d0fc6604d83fd0

If the build path is set, we assume it is being shared
and therefore we cannot check for applications as we
may have both false positives and false negatives.

Therefore we let the application that owns the build path
to ultimately perform the check.

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-11-16 18:41:22 +0100
**Commit:** ba79d29aa5a81655378d08cf0f632fb0d7d51b7e

Note a field named safe_by_default has been added so we don't
warn on variables defined inside EXPR in "case EXPR, do: ...".

The proper solution would be to convert && and || into special
forms and they would be free of the warning. However,
safe_by_default is a welcome temporary solution until we see
how the warning will fare on actual applications.

### Merge pull request #3907 from Gazler/fix/umbrella-empty-dir

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-10-23 23:38:39 +0200
**Commit:** 49e7b8a8b8b08aa4a191382d3cf15fbfa6d3f3d4

fix(Mix.Dep.Umbrella): prevent error when app is missing mix.exs
----

### fix(Mix.Dep.Umbrella): prevent error when app is missing mix.exs

**Author:** Gary Rennie <gazler@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2015-10-23 22:19:52 +0100
**Commit:** 82d3da0774f27fa7ce0249d8a1a7b195cf17f0ba

Previously, when using an umbrella app, if a directory was empty when
running a mix task the following error was displayed:

 > ** (Mix) Could not find a Mix.Project, please ensure a mix.exs file
 > is available"

Since git does not keep directories, it is common to see this issue when
switching branches on an umbrella application where some branches have a
particular app inside `apps` and other branches don't.

This commit checks for the presence of `mix.exs` and uses directories
containing the file as an app in the umbrella application

### Allow size and map key variable matching in for and fn

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-10-21 13:10:31 +0200
**Commit:** ccb78d65e7cdf8c247b8e9b75f1c09c932bfeec9

We are treating map keys as patterns, so the pin
operator is required when matching on those.

We are treating bitstring specifiers as values,
so the pin operator is not required when matching
on those.

It is debatable if bitstring specifiers should
also be considered matches and require the pin
operator in such occasions, the reason why we have
decided to keep it as value is two fold:

1. Elixir 1.0 used them as values, so it is
   backwards compatible;

2. Supporting them as patterns introduces
   ambiguity since they are never matched,
   for example, we would need to write:

     x = 8
     <<a, b::size(^x)>> # valid
     <<x, y::size(x)>>  # valid
     <<a, b::size(x)>>  # invalid

   The last example contradicts regular matching
   where it would be valid with or without the pin
   operator. Notice this problem does not occur with
   maps because maps can never bind on a variable
   introduced in the pattern itself.

----

### Introduce String.trim_{prefix,suffix,leading,trailing}/2

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2015-10-18 01:15:51 +0200
**Commit:** ecf90268eb1e4acb8b104325524c6f12746caa7f

The first two will remove only the first occurrence of
the given match in string. The last two will remove all
occurrences of the given match.

We have chosen the leading/trailing naming instead of
left/right because left/right is used in String as
lstrip/rstrip and ljust/rjust, i.e. with a different
naming convention. Furthermore, the strip/just variants
receives codepoints while the ones in trim receives
strings themselves.

### [#3707] Warn when @attributes are redefined

**Author:** Daniel Berkompas <himself@danielberkompas.com>
**Date:** 2015-09-28 11:36:30 -0700
**Commit:** 50e37d75e0b60b0e859b5f6a4304f7b8f2a43161

Attributes such as @doc and @moduledoc should emit warnings when they
are redefined. For example:

```
@doc “first”
@doc “second”
```

This should emit a warning to the user, because the doc tag will be
overwritten with the value “second”.

See #3707 for more details.

the code produced previously:

  [var] = case(right) do

      #...
      [var]
    _ ->
      #...
  end

  [var, var] = case(right) do
    {var, var} ->
      #...
      [var, var]
    _ ->
      #...

### Reject non fullfilled optional dependencies later on

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2016-02-17 00:05:59 +0100
**Commit:** c3582f961713363c3e8a4587f932f306da5d34bf

Imagine this dependency tree:

    * parent
      * child
        * ecto
        * postgrex
      * ja_serializer
        * ecto

where postgrex is an optional dependency of Ecto.

Because optional dependencies were rejected later on,
ecto would have its postgrex dependency stripped and
later failed to top-sort. This commit changes it to
so optional dependencies are rejected only later on.

Signed-off-by: José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>

### Fix a possible binary leak in Integer.parse/1

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-02 09:35:25 +0100
**Commit:** 173c57fed2f6399b8d4964cd25bef4ac8c1c27ee

Integer.parse/1 followed this pattern:

    defp do_parse(<<char, rest :: binary>>, ...) do
      ...
      # instead of re-using the original binary, we do this
      {..., <<char, rest :: binary>>}
    end

This causes a new binary to be created instead of `rest` just being a
sub-binary.

Signed-off-by: José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>

----

**Date:** 2016-04-13 12:53:34 +0200
**Commit:** 3798dff0fca55b2a486581257831e3830e770f72

Prior to this commit, an Elixir file that did not
generate any modules would always be regenerated
whenever mix compile was invoked.

This commit addresses this issue by keeping source
files on its own rows in the Elixir manifest.

### Document change in behavior of `Enum.group_by` ordering. (#4794)

**Author:** Myron Marston <myron.marston@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-06-09 11:40:11 -0700
**Commit:** a1bbc1bc207fb936de7c8241faf223b415fb1308

On 1.2, here's how `group_by` behaved:

    iex(1)> 1..10 |> Enum.group_by(fn i -> i < 5 end)
    %{false: [10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5], true: [4, 3, 2, 1]}

On 1.3, here's how it behaves:

    iex(1)> 1..10 |> Enum.group_by(fn i -> i < 5 end)
    %{false: [5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10], true: [1, 2, 3, 4]}

### Use heuristic for compiler errors (#4778)

**Author:** Gary Rennie <gazler@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-06-04 15:31:37 +0100
**Commit:** a0c0cb6358ba0577ed9f5f5f529e1868134a5893

Previously when all files being compiled get stuck waiting on
something else, we would release those files in random order.

This commit changes this to release files in groups based on
the module they are waiting on. We pick the module being
depended on with less edges, as it is mostly likely being the
cause of conflict. This may not always be true though: for example,
if there is a macro injecting code into multiple modules and such
code becomes faulty, now multiple modules are waiting on
this same module.

However, we have to pick one or the other, and we
decided to pick the one with fewer dependencies.

### ApplicationTest fails under Windows (#4761)

**Author:** robi-wan <robi-wan@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2016-06-03 01:53:26 +0200
**Commit:** e4e0f2d63346fb6c6e8cddc5e2310400f51bab5f

2) test application directory (ApplicationTest)
     test/elixir/application_test.exs:53
     Assertion with == failed
     code: String.downcase(Application.app_dir(:elixir)) == String.downcase(Path.join(root, "bin/../lib/elixir"))
     lhs:  "d:/home/docs/dev/git_repos/robi-wan-elixir/lib/elixir"
     rhs:  "d:/home/docs/dev/git_repos/robi-wan-elixir/bin/../lib/elixir"
     stacktrace:
       test/elixir/application_test.exs:55: (test)

`Application.app_dir(:elixir)` delivers under Windows (7 Pro 64bit) an absolute path:

iex(1)> Application.app_dir(:elixir)
"d:/home/docs/dev/git_repos/robi-wan-elixir/lib/elixir"

Under Linux (Ubuntu 16.04 64bit) it delivers a relative path:

iex(1)> Application.app_dir(:elixir)
"/home/robi-wan/development/work/robi-wan-elixir/bin/../lib/elixir"

`Application.app_dir/1` uses `:code.lib_dir` to retrieve the code path.
So maybe the different types of paths (relative vs absolute) are caused by Erlang.

Suggestion to fix the tests under Windows: Use Path.expand/1 to convert
the path (on the right hand side of the assertion) to an absolute path.

### Clarify the use of `async: true` (#4692)

**Author:** Stephen Ball <sdball@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-05-27 02:51:48 -0400
**Commit:** aad62afb2e4844e817e2430af94eef5035b79949

The documentation here was a bit confusingly worded to make it sound
like with `async: true` each `test` declaration in the case would run
asynchronously. I've tried to reword it and make it clear that the flag
is set for the test case itself.

One example of the confusion is issue #3580. I found that thread when
trying to find the same answer for why six tests with
`:timer.sleep(1000)` were running in serial within a single test case.

### Keep brackets in the authority of URIs for IPv6 hosts

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-05-26 11:33:20 +0200
**Commit:** f3d938d0750c0376c7b54afa3b9aaa4e6b83fd78

Right now, when parsing a URI, we strip square brackets out of
hosts (meaning they're IPv6 hosts) and then use the stripped host to
rebuild the authority that will end up in the %URI{} struct. This means
that, for example:

    URI.parse("foo://[::]:1234").authority == ":::1234"

which is not good. In this commit, I fixed this by not rebuilding the
authority using the new host in URI.parse/1. The authority will now
include brackets around the host, but the :host field in the %URI{}
struct is still stripped.

### Use square brackets for IPv6 in URI.to_string/1

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-05-25 16:13:27 +0200
**Commit:** 0fa88d8d16beef927eb4d2030419ac785e72b4b9

According to the grammar at
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#appendix-A, a host can have colons
in it only if it's a "IPv6" or a "IPvFuture"; in both cases, it's
expected to be surrounded by square brackets. This means that when
converting a URI to a string in URI.to_string/1, we can simply surround
a host with square brackets if it contains one or more colons.

### Fix failing doctest for Path.expand/1 under windows.

**Author:** robi-wan <robi-wan@suyu.de>
**Date:** 2016-05-19 00:28:09 +0200
**Commit:** 8997b632d3721f7e685b98be45f5e7e4ce946611

Test fails with this message:

     test doc at Path.expand/1 (11) (PathTest)
     test/elixir/path_test.exs:6
     Doctest failed
     code: Path.expand("/foo/bar/../bar") === "/foo/bar"

Remove iex> to disable this doctest.

### Fix failing test "expand path with user home" for Path.expand under Windows.

**Author:** robi-wan <robi-wan@suyu.de>
**Date:** 2016-05-19 00:04:45 +0200
**Commit:** 43a91beb1707a15dc65886fc5c4d110dad578acf

Test fails with this message:

     test expand path with user home (PathTest)
     test/elixir/path_test.exs:113
     Assertion with == failed
     code: home == Path.expand("~")
     lhs:  "C:\\Users\\username"
     rhs:  "c:/Users/username"
     stacktrace:
       test/elixir/path_test.exs:118: (test)

'home' is the value of 'System.user_home!' which uses
':elixir_config.get(:home)' which gets this value set from the call to
'init:get_argument(home)'.

Erlang delivers the user home with back slashes.
Path.expand/1 uses Path.absname/2 which converts the back slashes into slashes.

Simple fix: Compute 'home' using Path.absname/1

----

### Fix failing test "relative win" for Path.relative_to/2 under windows

**Author:** robi-wan <robi-wan@suyu.de>
**Date:** 2016-05-18 23:42:20 +0200
**Commit:** 8c836eb78bb7f40e0483be8d25e688d178e62e8b

Test fails with this message:

     test relative win (PathTest)
     test/elixir/path_test.exs:36
     Assertion with == failed
     code: Path.relative_to("D:/usr/local/foo", "d:") == "usr/local/foo"
     lhs:  "D:/usr/local/foo"
     rhs:  "usr/local/foo"
     stacktrace:
       test/elixir/path_test.exs:48: (test)

Path.relative_to/2 uses :filename.split/1 - split returns a drive letter with a trailing slash
(http://erlang.org/doc/man/filename.html#split-1)

iex(1)> Path.split("D:/usr/local/foo")
["d:/", "usr", "local", "foo"]
iex(2)> Path.split("D:")
["d:"]
iex(3)> Path.split("D:/")
["d:/"]

So the second argument needs a trailing slash to strip the drive information from given path.

### Windows: batch file improvements (#4642)

**Author:** robi-wan <robi-wan@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2016-05-18 22:22:41 +0200
**Commit:** 501f856a23d67de69adb106718bcd6b9a942df7d

* Add usage information to iex.bat

Support command line switch '--help', '-h', '/h' and '/?' to show usage information for iex.bat.
Check argument with '/I' to make the test case insensitive:
This allows showing usage information with '--HELP', '-H' and '/H'.

Use 'setlocal' and 'endlocal' so changes to the environment are local to the batch file
(https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/library/bb491001.aspx) - so there is no need to un-set __ELIXIR_IEX_FLAGS.

* Use documented syntax 'goto label' - without leading colon before the label

* Support cli switch '/?' to show help

Use label :end to jump to the end of the batch file after showing help text -
so the call to elixir.bat is not executed when showing help.

Use 'setlocal' and 'endlocal' so that the env var 'argc' is local to this batch file.

* Support cli switch '/?' to show help for elixir.bat

Test for cli switch '/?' does not need to be case insensitive.

### Always add an environment and print it alongside the dep

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2016-05-18 11:27:03 +0200
**Commit:** eced1303efd2622f5080949290bdd9dc9b92c893

There are two fixes here:

* All dependencies run in a particular environment, which defaults
  to prod. If two dependencies have different environments, they
  will diverge but the error message wouldn't include the env flag,
  which made it hard to spot the reason. This commit now always
  include the :env option

* Our converger algorithm was comparing [env: :prod] with [] and
  accusing a divergence but they should be the same as the default
  :env is :prod. We have made sure to set the environment to :prod
  for all deps

### Friendly error message for duplicate ExUnit test names (#4613)

**Author:** Jay Hayes <jay@bignerdranch.com>
**Date:** 2016-05-13 09:17:54 -0500
**Commit:** e3443b9919c0223bc0ef47dfecbd3fcdd1ba69fc

Previously, duplicate test names would output a warning like:

  warning: this clause cannot match because a previous clause at line 6 always matches

In order to understand the warning, the user had know that ExUnit defines
functions based on the test names. This was an implementation detail that the
user shouldn't have to know about. Since the second test definition is useless,
make the definition of it fail immediately without running the tests and
explicitly tell the user why. The new error looks like:

  ** (ExUnit.DuplicateTestError) A test named "foo" is already defined in Elixir.DupTest.
      test/dup_test.exs:6: (module)
      (stdlib) erl_eval.erl:670: :erl_eval.do_apply/6

### IO: Several improvements (#4560)

**Author:** eksperimental <eksperimental@users.noreply.github.com>
**Date:** 2016-04-28 06:18:32 -0500
**Commit:** a70effd4b4367775f348b7d0c2e1a5c33ccc0dbd

IO Module:
  * Impoves wording in documentation, particularly in the use of :all, :line, count
  * Standardizes arg names to be `line_*`.
  * Adds function guards to check for integers.
  * Unicode is a proper noun, so it should be always capitalized.
  * Adds backticks to args suchs as `device`, `item`, `count`.
  * When functions are "Unicode unsafe", they are indicated in the first paragraph of docs.
  * IO.puts: code simplified removing unnecessary variable.
  * Adds \n to example in IO.gets/2
  * Adds example in IO.chardata_to_string/1 when dealing with strings
  * Renames args in IO.each_stream/2 and IO.each_binstream/2
  * Adds tests for IO.getn/2-3 calling functions with different arities

IO.Steam Module:
  * Adds a note about side effects when dealing with IO streams.

### Remove the use of the word `pad` from chunk

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2016-04-25 19:54:15 +0200
**Commit:** f266c5d5331b4091d65e88d267562c50226bb56b

We will now take the word `pad` to mean something used for
completion and cycled until the number of desired elements
are given.

Given this is not the behaviour in `chunk`, we renamed the
argument from `pad` to `leftover`.

This patch does not change the behaviour, it just amends
the documentation to use proper names.

### Handle chars literals in the parser for better syntax errors

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-04-04 21:35:12 +0200
**Commit:** 51feaa5e621b8c17eb0a06da16f45756b6fdb566

Handle chars literals in the parser for better syntax errors
----

### Handle chars literals in the parser for better syntax errors

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-28 17:58:23 +0200
**Commit:** 8619d26c4d8001ea52d9382ced0ddd1af4a80add

Before this commit, we handled char literals (like `?a`) in the
tokenizer, turning a literal like `?a` into the token `{:number, _,
97}` (thus indistinguishable from the literal `97` at the parsing
stage). This led to error messages with the integer for the character
instead of the character literal, e.g.:

    iex> :ok ?a
    ** (SyntaxError) iex:11: syntax error before: 97

With this commit, we now turn `?a` into the token `{:char, _,
97}` (which is the same token used by Erlang for Erlang char literals
like `$a`); since it's the same token as in Erlang, the parser will now
output the char literal as an Erlang char (`?a` would be printed as
`$a`). We hijack the error message in elixir_errors.erl to end up with
the correct message:

    iex> :ok ?a
    ** (SyntaxError) iex:11: syntax error before: ?a

### Improve merge exception texts inside exunit callbacks

**Author:** azhi <astzhe@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-30 02:14:01 +0300
**Commit:** 410e2299deacb391202797122b794214ca9f4626

Considering this case:

```elixir
defmodule CallbacksCase do
  use ExUnit.Case

  setup do
    {:ok, :something}
  end

  test "nothing", do: assert true
end
```

Before this commit exunit callbacks return value merger was failing with

`(RuntimeError) expected ExUnit callback in CallbacksCase to return :ok or
{:ok, keyword | map}, got :something instead`.

But callback didn't return `:something`, it returned `{:ok, something}`.

After this commit same case will fail with

`(RuntimeError) expected ExUnit callback in CallbacksCase to return :ok or
{:ok, keywords | map}, got {:ok, :something} instead`.

This behaviour is achieved by moving all the checks to `__merge__/3` function.
`context_merge/3` now only works with maps and raises 'reserved keys' errors.

### Merge pull request #4450 from whatyouhide/anonymous-functions-in-pipes

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-30 13:53:42 +0200
**Commit:** 8e8336b75f30b48ccb972d50709eabb72ef33ac4

Handle non-called anonymous functions in Macro.pipe/3
----

### Handle non-called anonymous functions in Macro.pipe/3

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-30 11:22:17 +0200
**Commit:** 2faab1db7db59cfc2216be0fba9eab1c8951c677

Right now, this nasty error pops out:

    iex> :foo |> (fn x -> x end)
    ** (CompileError) iex:1: expected -> clauses in fn

This happens because of what we do in `Macro.pipe/3`, which is: we take
the AST of a function call as the second argument and insert the first
argument in the list of arguments for the function call, at the position
specified by the third argument. The AST for a `fn` looks exactly like
the AST of a function call (to the `:fn` function):

    iex> quote do: fn :ok -> :ok; :err -> :err end
    {:fn, [], [{:->, [], [[:ok], :ok]}, {:->, [], [[:error], :error]}]}

It's easy to see that the "arguments" to `:fn` are the `->` clauses in
the function. This means that doing `:foo |> (fn x -> x end)` basically
adds another clause to the function:

    iex> Macro.pipe(:foo, quote(do: fn :ok -> :ok; :err -> :err end), 0)
    {:fn, [], [:foo, {:->, [], [[:ok], :ok]}, {:->, [], [[:err], :err]}]}

and this makes `:elixir_fn.expand/3` blow up because it doesn't know how
to handle the `:foo` clause (because it's not a clause!).

With this commit, we blow up early in `Macro.pipe/3` when we see a
`{:fn, _, _}` call:

    iex> :foo |> (fn x -> x end)
    ** (ArgumentError) cannot pipe :foo into an anonymous function
    without calling the function; use :foo |> (fn x -> x end).()

Suppress unused var warnings when removing Logger macros from the AST

### Add some comments to the Logger module

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-29 23:16:43 +0200
**Commit:** 7c5fa9a3b728d6ba09de1938cdcca149f004deee

### Suppress unused var warnings when removing Logger macros from the AST

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-27 11:32:07 +0200
**Commit:** a2885e26108584e328f38a5ed2d743229afa545e

Right now, code like this:

    defmodule MyMod do
      require Logger
      def my_fun(arg) do
        Logger.debug(arg)
        :ok
      end
    end

will generate an unused variable warning for the `arg` variable in
`my_fun/1` if the log level is higher than :debug. This happens because
in such cases, we completely remove the AST of the Logger call, so the
`arg` variable is effectively never used. This may seem magical to the
user.

With this commit, a Logger call which would have been removed from the
AST before now generates a series of `_ = x` expressions, one for each
variable passed to the Logger macro.

### Merge pull request #4444 from whatyouhide/aliases-in-pipes

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-29 20:16:47 +0200
**Commit:** 8594b7115c0784c199833b5b98479af411498bb8

Error out when passing :__aliases__ to Macro.pipe/3
----

### Error out when passing :__aliases__ to Macro.pipe/3

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-29 19:47:54 +0200
**Commit:** 7e77c913203ec61b09de139a9dedd61d125c54a0

Right now, this funny thing happens:

    iex> Macro |> Env
    Macro.Env

This happens because `|>/2` calls `Macro.pipe/3` under the hood, and
`Macro.pipe/3` inserts the left-hand side at the beginning of the list
of arguments in the AST for the function call on the right-hand
side. Aliases, however, look exactly like a call to the __aliases__
function:

    iex> quote do: Macro.Env
    {:__aliases__, [alias: false], [:Macro, :Env]}

and that's why `Macro |> Env` becomes `Macro.Env`. With this commit, we
explicitly take care of `:__aliases__` in a `Macro.pipe/3` call, so that
we can error out in such cases:

    iex> Macro |> Env
    ** (ArgumentError) cannot pipe Macro into Env, ...

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-02 19:52:13 +0100
**Commit:** 7a82caea342cba2e5a2b36e8eef815d10f205d0c

Fix a possible binary leak in Integer.parse/1
----

### Fix a possible binary leak in Integer.parse/1

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-03-02 09:35:25 +0100
**Commit:** 45d5d32e30bfe5333c3c38bedeed6419e81a5cb1

Integer.parse/1 followed this pattern:

    defp do_parse(<<char, rest :: binary>>, ...) do
      ...
      # instead of re-using the original binary, we do this
      {..., <<char, rest :: binary>>}
    end

This causes a new binary to be created instead of `rest` just being a
sub-binary.

### Merge pull request #4340 from wojtekmach/import_warnings

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-02-28 20:31:07 +0100
**Commit:** 17368eb956637adc6c5a7f4df2cc2ac69a74f390

Track {module, function, arity} imports and warn on unused ones
----

### Track {module, function, arity} imports and warn on unused ones

**Author:** Wojtek Mach <wojtek@wojtekmach.pl>
**Date:** 2016-02-27 20:20:41 +0100
**Commit:** 743e8c7ed12ea71062d8b51164ec00ffcd92ecf5

Example:

Say, there's following file:

    # example.exs
    import String, only: [upcase: 1, downcase: 1]
    import Enum

    IO.puts upcase("Hello")

Before this patch:

    # $ elixir example.exs
    # HELLO
    # warning.exs:2: warning: unused import Enum

After this patch:

    # $ elixir example.exs
    # HELLO
    # example.exs:1: warning: unused import String.downcase/1
    # example.exs:2: warning: unused import Enum

### Refer to the revision in mix.exs when updating deps

**Author:** Andrea Leopardi <an.leopardi@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-02-24 19:05:08 +0100
**Commit:** c77a1b2f62e13c01d60bc6322aaf464fe44dd8a4

Before this commit, we were correctly flagging a lock file as outdated
when the rev (branch/tag/rev) had been updated in mix.exs; at checkout
time, though, we were still looking at the lock file before looking at
mix.exs. Now, when checking out we look at mix.exs first and then fall
back to the lock file.

This should close #4309.

### Reject non fullfilled optional dependencies later on

**Author:** José Valim <jose.valim@plataformatec.com.br>
**Date:** 2016-02-17 00:05:59 +0100
**Commit:** 68d5d9c07bf27889c71272dbd6fe350977ce110b

Imagine this dependency tree:

    * parent
      * child
        * ecto
        * postgrex
      * ja_serializer
        * ecto

where postgrex is an optional dependency of Ecto.

Because optional dependencies were rejected later on,
ecto would have its postgrex dependency stripped and
later failed to top-sort. This commit changes it to
so optional dependencies are rejected only later on.

### Support :base option when inspecting binaries

**Author:** Dmitry Kakurin <dmitry.kakurin@gmail.com>
**Date:** 2016-02-13 23:03:30 -0800
**Commit:** 5e272b8c10088d57a9090a80ed1a28287d3e80fd

Allow inspecting binaries as :hex or :octal.

Examples:

# as before
iex> inspect("abc")
"\"abc\""

# as before
iex> inspect("abc", binaries: :as_binary)
"<<97, 98, 99>>"

# NEW: base: :hex is recognized
iex> inspect("abc", binaries: :as_binary, base: :hex)
"<<0x61, 0x62, 0x63>>"

# NEW: any base other than :decimal implies binaries: :as_binaries
iex> inspect("abc", base: :hex)
"<<0x61, 0x62, 0x63>>"
iex> inspect("abc", base: :octal)
"<<0o141, 0o142, 0o143>>"

# NOTE: size is still represented as decimal
iex> inspect(<< 10, 11, 12::4 >>, base: :hex)
"<<0xA, 0xB, 0xC::size(4)>>"
